claims.title: Choosing the second place before the level
claims.hypotheses: The CM arithmetic datum has an integral quadratic generator of negative discriminant, a geometric prime p, a first split place carrying the cuspidal type and finite forbidden rational and level supports.
claims.statement: There is a good odd rational prime r away from all prescribed bad places and a nonempty choice W of exactly one member of each conjugate pair above r. The same r and W precede all admissible levels divisible by r.

claims.title: Why does every matrix in the double coset have distinct eigenvalues in the local field?
claims.hypotheses: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with uniformizer π and its normalized valuation. I is the upper Iwahori in GLₙ(K) and the integers b₀,…,bₙ₋₁ are strictly decreasing.
claims.statement: Every matrix in I diag(π^{b_i}) I has a split characteristic polynomial with one simple root of each valuation bᵢ.

claims.title: How does a Hecke product stay in a double coset with regular spectrum?
claims.hypotheses: The subgroup I reduces to the upper triangular subgroup modulo the maximal ideal. The diagonal t has strictly decreasing exponents. Hecke functions are bi-invariant with finite double-coset support.
claims.statement: Put Xₘ=ItᵐI. Then X₁Xₘ is contained in Xₘ₊₁. A nonzero convolution value is a sum with at least one nonzero summand, so the same containment propagates the support of positive powers.

claims.title: Why is the local test invertible on fixed vectors?
claims.hypotheses: The residue field of the local field is finite, the coefficient field is complex, the Iwahori subgroup has Haar volume one and the diagonal exponents are weakly decreasing.
claims.statement: The indicator of the diagonal double coset acts invertibly on Iwahori-fixed vectors and admits a left convolution inverse in the local Hecke algebra.

claims.title: Clearing denominators without losing regular support
claims.hypotheses: Use the odd-rank compact unitary setup, an admissible level divisible by r, the cuspidal type and independent Iwahori factors at the places of W. Let Λ denote the integral lattice away from p. Normalize convolution by the principal level.
claims.statement: The type corner contains u with e∗u=u∗e=u and a Hecke function u′ satisfies u′∗u=e. For every m≥1, any nonzero value of fₘ=u^{∗m}∗e at g has g⁻¹Λ contained in Λ and dᵐpr_w(g) in I_w t_wᵐ I_w at every w∈W.

claims.title: Transporting regular support to the orbital terms
claims.hypotheses: Keep the centrally translated powers and the observed Hecke functions whose supports project into the local Iwahori groups. The frame identifies the split matrix factors, and the CM conjugate factors satisfy the similitude relation.
claims.statement: Every word-polynomial left multiplier preserves the local support restriction. The characteristic polynomial is separable at the second split realization. At conjugate places the nonzero eigenvalues transform by λ↦ν/λ, giving a commutative centralizer at the rational place.

claims.title: Choosing one power for the nonzero definite trace
claims.hypotheses: Fix a seen eigenvalue system θ in the type image of the finite-dimensional space of definite forms. On that image the observations commute with one another and with the injective action of u.
claims.statement: There are one polynomial projector A and one integer m≥1 such that, for every word polynomial s, the total definite trace of (As)(ψ)fₘ is s(θ) times the nonzero power trace of Bᵐ on the joint generalized θ-space.
